```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(farsr)
# The FARS files shipped with the package are read from the working directory
data_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "farsr")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = data_dir)
```

## What the package does

`farsr` works with the data of the US National Highway Traffic Safety
Administration's Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS), a nationwide census
of fatal injuries in motor vehicle crashes. The package includes the yearly
files for 2013, 2014 and 2015 in `inst/extdata`. It has five main functions:

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fars_read()` | reads one FARS file into a tibble |
| `make_filename()` | builds the name of the file of a year |
| `fars_read_years()` | reads the month and year of the accidents of several years |
| `fars_summarize_years()` | counts the accidents by month and year |
| `fars_map_state()` | maps the accidents of a state in a year |

All functions look for the data files in the working directory. The files are
named `accident_<year>.csv.bz2`.

## Reading a file

```{r read}
accidents_2013 <- fars_read("accident_2013.csv.bz2")
dim(accidents_2013)
head(accidents_2013[, c("STATE", "MONTH", "DAY", "FATALS")])
```

`make_filename()` gives the file name of a year, and does not check that the
file exists:

```{r filename}
make_filename(2014)
```

## Accidents per month and year

`fars_summarize_years()` returns one row per month and one column per year:

```{r summarize}
fars_summarize_years(c(2013, 2014, 2015))
```

A year without a data file gives a warning and is left out of the table:

```{r invalid}
res <- suppressWarnings(fars_read_years(c(2013, 1999)))
sapply(res, is.null)
```

## Mapping the accidents of a state

`fars_map_state()` takes the state code used in the `STATE` column and a year.
State 1 is Alabama:

```{r map, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5}
fars_map_state(1, 2013)
```

A state code that is not in the data stops with the error
`invalid STATE number`.
